findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw, unparsed fetch Response while the normal refresh path returns an already-parsed SDK/axios response, breaking callers when credential sync is enabled
findings.body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, refreshOAuthTokens() returns the raw `fetch()` Response object from hitting CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. However, several callers assume the shape returned by their normal (non-sync) refresh function, which is NOT a raw fetch Response (e.g. googlecalendar's googleapis client returns `fetchTokens.res` with a `.data` property, hubspot's SDK returns a parsed token object with `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken`, and zoho-bigin/zohocrm use axios which returns `{ data: ... }`). When sync is enabled the function instead returns a bare fetch Response, which has no `.data` property and is not the SDK's parsed object. Any code path that reads `res.data`, `.expiresIn`, etc. on the sync-enabled branch will get `undefined` and throw a TypeError (or silently produce NaN/garbage values), meaning the credential-sync feature is broken for every app except those whose non-sync refresh function itself performs a raw `fetch()` (office365calendar, office365video, webex, zoomvideo, lark). This is a core correctness bug in the feature this PR implements.

findings.title: Google Calendar token refresh breaks when credential sync is enabled: `res?.data` is undefined for the sync branch
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with a refresh function that returns `fetchTokens.res` (an object with `.data`) in the non-sync case. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, refreshOAuthTokens instead returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data` property. The subsequent line `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token` will throw a TypeError at runtime, so enabling app credential sync for Google Calendar will crash token refresh entirely instead of working as advertised in the PR.

findings.title: HubSpot token refresh breaks when credential sync is enabled due to response shape mismatch
findings.body: In the non-sync branch, `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` resolves directly to a parsed HubspotToken object (with `.expiresIn`, `.accessToken`, etc.). When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` instead returns the raw `fetch()` Response from the sync endpoint. The code immediately does `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn * 1000)` and `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken)`, both of which will be `undefined`/`NaN` on a raw Response object, since Response has no `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` fields. The same shape-mismatch pattern also affects `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, which read `tokenInfo.data...` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data...` assuming an axios-style response, but get a raw fetch Response when sync is enabled.

findings.title: Missing `prisma` import causes compile/runtime failure in Salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: The new `getClient` method calls `await prisma.credential.update({...})`, but the file never imports `prisma` (e.g. `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`). This is a plain reference error that should fail TypeScript type-checking and will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime, breaking every Salesforce calendar operation (create/update/delete event, availability) since `getClient` is invoked unconditionally from the constructor.

findings.title: Salesforce access token is refreshed on every CalendarService instantiation with no expiry check
findings.body: Unlike other providers (hubspot, zoho-bigin, zohocrm, office365, zoomvideo, webex), the new Salesforce `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to Salesforce's OAuth token endpoint every time a `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed, regardless of whether the current access token is still valid. There is no `isTokenValid`/expiry check guarding the refresh call. This causes unnecessary refresh-token round trips on every booking operation, risking rate limiting and unnecessary rotation of refresh tokens (some OAuth providers invalidate the previous refresh token on each refresh, which under concurrent requests could cause race conditions where one request's refresh token becomes stale before it is persisted). Additionally, this refresh call does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce credential syncing (the stated purpose of this PR) is not actually wired up for this app despite other apps being updated.

findings.title: Computed property keys using `.toString()` do not implement the intended catch-all schema
findings.body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to define a dynamic/catch-all schema using `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. Calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema instance does not return a dynamic field name pattern; it returns the default `Object.prototype.toString()` value (e.g. "[object Object]") for both expressions. As both computed keys evaluate to the identical literal string, the second definition silently overwrites the first in the object literal, so the resulting schema is effectively just `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`. The intended behavior (treat any numeric property as an expiry field and accept arbitrary other properties) is never implemented, meaning the 'minimum' schema used when credential sync is enabled does not actually validate token expiry fields are present at all; it's dead code that would pass validation for payloads completely missing any expiry information.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws unconditionally on invalid tokens, changing previously tolerant error handling in Office365
findings.body: Previously, office365calendar's refresh flow used `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` directly and, on failure, logged the Zod error plus the raw MS response and continued gracefully (merging only successfully-parsed fields, keeping the stale credentials). The new shared `parseRefreshTokenResponse` helper throws an `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` whenever parsing fails, and the office365 diagnostic `console.error` logging of the zod error / MS response was removed. This changes office365's refresh behavior from a soft, loggable failure to a hard throw, and removes debugging visibility into why Microsoft's token response failed validation — a regression for an existing, unrelated code path incidental to this feature.

findings.title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time and HTTP method is not validated
findings.body: The webhook secret check at line 24-29 uses a plain `!==` string comparison between the incoming header and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, which is vulnerable to timing attacks that could let an attacker incrementally guess the secret. Additionally, the handler never checks `req.method`, so GET/PUT/DELETE requests are processed the same as POST; combined with no `defaultHandler`/`defaultResponder` wrapper used elsewhere in the codebase, malformed non-POST requests will hit `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` with an undefined body and throw an unhandled exception instead of a clean 400 response.

findings.title: symmetricDecrypt call is not wrapped in try/catch
findings.body: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)` followed by `JSON.parse(...)` can throw if the payload is malformed or was encrypted with a different key. There is no try/catch around this, so a bad request results in an unhandled exception / generic 500 instead of a clear validation error, making it harder for self-hosters to diagnose integration issues with their own sync service.

findings.title: Hardcoded redirect URI slug diverges from callback.ts which still uses appConfig.slug
findings.body: This PR changes `add.ts`'s redirect_uri from the templated `` `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` `` to a hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`, while `callback.ts` in the same app still builds its redirect_uri dynamically from `appConfig.slug`. Although the value happens to be identical today, this inconsistency is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and makes the two files diverge silently if the app slug ever changes, risking a redirect_uri mismatch between the authorization request and the token exchange.

findings.title: No automated tests for the new credential-sync webhook or OAuth refresh/credential utilities
findings.body: The PR adds a new, security-sensitive webhook endpoint (`app-credential.ts`) plus shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) that affect token refresh for ~10 apps, but ships with no unit or integration tests (the author explicitly checked 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective'). Given the response-shape bugs identified in refreshOAuthTokens consumers, tests covering both the sync-enabled and sync-disabled code paths would have caught these regressions before merge.
